battle.name: 藤原仲麻呂之亂
battle.brief: 天平神護八年九月，藤原仲麻呂舉兵佔領平城京，孝謙天皇出奔伊勢神宮；朝廷自七道徵發十四萬餘兵，於九月二十八日夜襲藤原京，叛軍潰散，首腦縛赴木津川沈氾。卡面羅馬重步兵並未參戰——相距七百餘年；但八世紀日本以弓為主的兵陣同樣靠步卒頂住前線，軍制則是徵兵而非常備軍團。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 叛軍一方以左大臣藤原仲麻呂為首，核心是藤原朝臣一族在平城京的公卿與近臣，以及聞訊而來的各國豪族首領；兵員主體是《新抄格勅符抄》所載的「七道百姓」，即伊勢、參河、駿河、遠江、紀伊、豊前、筑前等國的國司與國造依敕書應召的鄉村武裝，以弓手為主、輔以騎兵。叛軍佔據平城京的宮殿與都門，扣住詔令的發佈權，並遣人往伊勢方向企圖截斷朝廷的求援與集兵之路。王師一方以孝謙天皇（事後追尊稱德天皇）為大義所在，皇太子淳仁天皇居中策應，核心參謀是先前因反對立後而遭貶的藤原永手、藤原魚名等公卿，加上中務省直屬的左右衛門府與兵衛府的京畿兵、各國國司國造奉詔帶來的徵發兵與地方豪族民兵，以及伊勢神宮背書的神託。兩軍同屬律令國家的兵制框架：平時以屯倉與衛府常備兵維持秩序，戰時靠國司依敕書臨時徵集，兵員、馬匹、兵仗與糧食按國分攤，這一點直接決定了雙方集結與崩潰的速度。
countriesEn: The rising was fought between two coalitions inside the same ritsuryō state. On the rebel side stood the udaijin Fujiwara no Nakamaro at the head of the Fujiwara courtiers and close retainers of Heijō-kyō, together with provincial magnates who rode in when word got out; the bulk of his force was the people of the seven circuits recorded in the Shōsō kyakuchoku fushō — provincial warriors called up by the kokushi and kuni no miyatsuko of Ise, Mikawa, Suruga, Tōtōmi, Kii, Buzen and Chikuzen under imperial order, mostly archers with a body of horse. The rebels held the palace and the gates of Heijō-kyō, kept control of the issuing of edicts, and sent men toward Ise in a bid to cut the court's road for appeal and for mustering. On the court's side the cause was embodied by Empress Kōken (later Shōtoku Tennō), with Crown Prince Licinius holding the centre of the capital, and the strategy entrusted to Fujiwara no Nagate and Fujiwara no Uona, the very courtiers who had blocked Nakamaro's elevation and had been demoted for it. To them were added the capital-region troops of the Left and Right Gate Guards and the Defence Troops, the levies and private warriors brought in by provincial governors, and the backing of the Ise Grand Shrine through its oracle. Both armies nonetheless drew on the same ritsuryō framework: peacetime strength came from garrison farms and palace guards, wartime strength from levies summoned by written order, with men, horses, weapons and grain apportioned province by province — and it was this structure, far more than the generalship, that decided how fast each side could raise and then lose its army.
people: 藤原仲麻呂是此役的首謀者。他出自分封在藤原朝臣一支的藤原氏，母為尼當量，與光明中宮同出一門，歷仕聖武、孝謙兩朝，寶龜初年拜左大臣，掌朝廷實權。光明中宮於天平神護八年三月二十五日在平城京病逝，孝謙天皇一度有意立仲麻呂為中宮，經藤原永手、藤原魚名力勸而止，二人隨即被貶官外流，仲麻呂由此銜恨，轉而以手中兵權與門下公卿的支持向朝廷施壓。孝謙天皇是事件的另一方：她先退往近江，再入伊勢神宮、居於外宮二十餘日求取神託，然後以自己的尊位號召諸國出兵，詔書直點各國應到人數；其兄皇太子淳仁天皇留居京中，與永手、魚名等共謀應變。永手與魚名事後一度被放逐，直到宇多天皇承和二年（835）才正式復位。叛軍方面，光明中宮的禪師行信與近侍弓削御淨曾糾集僧兵與朝廷相抗，事敗被誅，顯示此役並非單純的公卿政變，而是同時牽動奈良後期的政教關係、門閥勢力與武人階層。
peopleEn: Fujiwara no Nakamaro was the architect of the rising. He belonged to the branch of the Fujiwara descended from Fujiwara no Asomi, was the son of the nun known as Nittō-shō and so a blood brother of Empress Kōmyō, the light of the court at Heijō-kyō. He served under Emperor Shōmu and Empress Kōken and was appointed udaijin in the early Hōki years, holding the substance of government. When Kōmyō died on the twenty-fifth day of the second month of Jingo 8 (25 March 764), Kōken briefly considered making Nakamaro her consort; Nagate and Uona argued against it and were demoted and sent away, and Nakamaro concluded from that moment that the court was set on destroying him. Kōken was the other party in person. She withdrew first toward Ōmi and then into the Outer Shrine of Ise, where she stayed more than twenty days seeking the divine oracle, and from there summoned the provinces in her own name, her edicts naming the men each province was to furnish. Her brother the crown prince remained in the capital, planning the response with Nagate, Uona and the others. Nagate and Uona spent years in exile before Emperor Uda restored them in Jōwa 2 (835). On the rebel side, Gyōshin, the Zen master of the late empress, and her attendant Yuge no Miyozumi even raised armed monks against the court and were executed when the scheme failed, showing that the rising was not a mere court intrigue but entangled the religious establishment, the aristocratic houses and the rising warrior class all at once.
kits: 本站為此役配上的兵器是羅馬重步兵，即前100年前後羅馬共和末期到帝國初期的重裝步卒：分段鎧甲、弧形大盾、短劍與標槍，以百人隊為基本單位編入軍團，兵役期長達二十年，靠糧秣輸送與連續營地維持戰鬥。必須說明：此戰發生於七六四年的日本，與羅馬相隔七百餘年、萬餘公里，現場沒有任何羅馬士兵，卡面兵器應視為同類兵種的標本，用來對照「重步兵」這一兵種的職能，而不是戰役的實物。真正上陣的裝備屬於奈良時代：以長弓配大矢為主的弓箭手最為普遍，一場會戰的勝負常由箭雨與遠程消耗決定；近身兵器是太刀與大刀，甲冑有短甲、大鎧，也有大鎧配橫矟太刀的樣式，步卒手持木製的楯與櫓，騎兵為披甲的騎馬與軍馬，後勤靠牛車與馬車輸送兵糧與箭筍，野營與城郭則用柵、拒馬以及斧、鉤、梯一類工具。與羅馬軍團相比，最大的分別是奈良時代的「兵」是依敕書臨時徵發的鄉村武裝，兵仗自備、訓練鬆散，臨陣才集合，軍紀與協同全靠主將的旗幟與號令維持。
kitsEn: The card for this battle carries the Roman legionary, the heavy infantryman of the late Republic and early Empire around 100 BC: segmentata armour, the curved scutum, the gladius and the pilum, formed into centuries within a legion, liable for twenty years of service and kept in the field by a chain of supply and a string of marching camps. It has to be said plainly that nothing Roman was present at Yamashiro in 764: the fighting in the Japanese capital took place more than seven centuries and some ten thousand kilometres away, so the card's weapon is best read as a specimen of that kind of heavy infantryman, useful for comparing what the arm actually did, and not as an artefact of the battle. What the soldiers of the Nara age actually carried is a different matter. Archery with the long bow and heavy arrows was by far the most widespread arm, and the issue of a single contest was usually settled by showers of arrows and long-range attrition; close combat was fought with tachi and ōdachi, covered by short and long armour, sometimes with the transverse tachi; footmen carried wooden shields and pavises, and the mounted arm fought in armour on garrison horses, with wagons carrying grain and bundles of arrows behind them, while palisades, chevaux-de-frise, axes, hooks and ladders served the camps and the works. The great difference from a Roman legion is that the soldiers of the Nara age were provincial levies called up by written order, equipped at their own expense, loosely trained and assembled only at the moment of need, cohesion maintained by the general's banners and orders rather than by drill.
tactics: 仲麻呂的戰法是先發制人：九月二十四日他控制平城京的宮殿與門禁，扣住詔令的發佈權，急召七道兵馬向畿內集中，企圖用兵力優勢迫使孝謙讓出後位甚至廢其皇位；同時遣人往伊勢，試圖切斷朝廷求援與集兵的通路。但徵兵的消息一旦走漏，七道之眾反成了朝廷的兵源：孝謙在伊勢發出的勅書直接點名各國應到人數，隊伍沿紀伊、伊勢、參河、駿河、遠江、豊前、筑前等道路向藤原京與近江方向集結，弓兵先到，騎兵與糧隊在後。王師把重點放在夜襲上：九月二十八日入夜後，朝廷軍自近江、越前等方向同時壓上，先以火把與火箭照亮叛軍陣地，弓兵齊射迫其亂陣，再由步卒與騎兵合擊，最後封鎖通往山地的道路，斷其退路。叛軍崩潰很快，營地焚毀，士卒各自逃散，逃到木津川一帶者或被殺或溺斃，數十名首腦被擒後在奧津沈氾處死。整場會戰只延續一夜，但追逐與搜捕持續數日，逃入山林的殘部才被逐一清剿。
tacticsEn: Nakamaro's method was the seizure of the capital first. On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month he took the palace and the gates of Heijō-kyō, kept control of the issuing of edicts, and hurried the levies of the seven circuits inward, hoping that sheer numbers would force Kōken to yield the consort's rank or the throne itself; at the same time he sent men toward Ise to cut the court's channel of appeal and of mustering. But once the summons leaked out, the levies of the seven circuits became the court's army instead. The edicts Kōken issued at Ise named the men each province was to furnish, and the columns moved along the roads from Kii, Ise, Mikawa, Suruga, Tōtōmi, Buzen and Chikuzen toward Fujiwara-kyō and Ōmi, the archers arriving first and the horse and the baggage trains behind them. The court concentrated everything on a night assault: after dark on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month the columns pressed in at the same moment from the Ōmi and Echizen directions, torches and fire-arrows lit the rebel positions, a volley from the archers disordered the formation, foot and horse then closed together to strike, and the roads into the hills were sealed to deny retreat. The rebel collapse was quick — the camp burned, the men scattered, those who reached the Kizu river were killed or drowned, and several dozen leaders were taken and drowned at the Oku-tsu of the same river. The battle itself lasted a single night, but the pursuit and the searching of the hills went on for days, and the remnants in the mountains were hunted down one by one.
data: 關於兵力的主要依據是《新抄格勅符抄》保存下來的徵發文書，記七道所出兵十四萬一千人、馬十萬疋有餘，並分列各國名額，例如常陸國五千四百二十八人、摂津國四千九百九十九人、筑前國三千五百七十五人、紀伊國三千零六十八人、伊勢國一千九百二十六人、遠江國七百一十人、參河國五百二十八人。這是八世紀律令朝廷的徵發額，不是點名冊上的實到人數，實際集結遠少於此，歷來研究者多視之為上限。戰役本身只延續一天：九月二十四日孝謙天皇離京，九月二十八日夜藤原京被攻破。叛軍首腦的處置記為「數十人」沈氾於木津川奧津，被殺與被俘的普通兵員數目無從考訂，只知逃散者死於河中與山野者甚多。藤原京在戰後焚毀，殿宇與官廨盡成焦土。作為對照，羅馬軍團在帝國時期常為五千至六千人，兵役二十年，裝備連同盾牌、鎧甲與行李約二十五至三十公斤，靠每日約二十公里的行軍與隨軍糧秣維持——這種常備化與計畫化的制度，正是奈良的徵兵隊伍所不具備的。
dataEn: The principal evidence for the numbers is the levy document preserved in the Shōsō kyakuchoku fushō, which records fourteen thousand one hundred men and more than a hundred thousand horses furnished by the seven circuits, with the quota of each province listed: Hitachi 5,428, Settsu 4,999, Chikuzen 3,575, Kii 3,068, Ise 1,926, Tōtōmi 710, Mikawa 528. These are levy quotas of the eighth-century ritsuryō government, not a muster roll of the men who actually turned up; the real gathering was far smaller, and historians generally treat the figure as an upper bound. The campaign itself lasted a single day: Kōken left the capital on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, and Fujiwara-kyō was carried by assault on the night of the twenty-eighth. The disposal of the rebel leaders is recorded as several dozen drowned at the Oku-tsu of the Kizu river; no figure survives for the common soldiers killed or taken, only the note that many of the fugitives died in the river and in the hills. Fujiwara-kyō burned afterwards, its halls and public offices reduced to cinders. By contrast, a Roman legion in the imperial period numbered around five to six thousand, served for twenty years, and carried on the order of twenty-five to thirty kilograms of shield, armour and baggage, sustained by a daily march of roughly twenty kilometres and by baggage trains with their grain — that standing, planned system is precisely what the levies of Nara did not have.
cause: 直接起因是七六四年三月二十五日光明中宮在平城京病逝。她的死抽走了奈良朝廷最核心的權力紐帶：她既是聖武天皇的正宮、孝謙天皇的生母，也是藤原氏在朝中的支柱。孝謙打算讓仲麻呂繼承後位，遭到永手、魚名反對並把二人貶謫，仲麻呂因此認定朝中有人要置自己於死地。更深一層是律令兵制的崩壞：兵衛與屯倉的常備軍早已空虛，國司與國造腐化成地方豪族，朝廷一旦有事，能迅速拉出來的只有靠鄉族關係維持的私兵；七道百姓的徵發方式、寺社的田宅與僧兵的存在，使任何一位握有兵權的公卿都可能舉兵。皇位繼承本身也有裂痕：孝謙無子，皇太子淳仁天皇由光明中宮撫養，藤原氏內部又分成擁立仲麻呂與擁護皇太子兩派。於是一場本可用一紙詔書解決的禮制糾紛，最終以七道十四萬人的徵發和一場夜襲收場。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the death of Empress Kōmyō at Heijō-kyō on the twenty-fifth day of the second month of 764. Her passing cut the central tie of the Nara court: she was at once the empress of Emperor Shōmu, the mother of Empress Kōken and the pillar of the Fujiwara inside the government. Kōken meant to let Nakamaro succeed to the consort's rank, and Nagate and Uona opposed it and were demoted for their part; Nakamaro from that moment believed the court was set on destroying him. Deeper down lay the collapse of the ritsuryō military system: the palace guards and the garrison farms had long been empty shells, the governors and district heads had turned into local magnates, and when the court had trouble the only thing it could call up quickly was private force held together by local family ties. The way the seven circuits were levied, the temple estates and the existence of armed monks meant that any magnate with troops at hand could rise. The succession itself was cracked too: Kōken had no child, the crown prince Licinius had been raised by Kōmyō, and inside the Fujiwara one faction favoured Nakamaro while another backed the crown prince. What should have been settled by a single edict about precedence at court ended instead with a levy of a hundred and forty thousand men and a battle fought at night.
impact: 此役是奈良時代的最後一場大規模內亂，直接改寫了往後十年的政局。朝廷以叛亂為由頒布崇儒貶佛之詔與僧尼還俗令，收寺田、迫僧尼還俗，平城京一帶的寺院受到清算，行信糾集僧兵反抗，事敗被誅，佛教在奈良朝廷的靠山一時崩塌；這套政策維持到宇多天皇承和二年（835）才被廢止，藤原永手、藤原魚名得以復位。人事上，藤原仲麻呂被捕後流放，先後配流於出雲與淡路，據《日本後紀》載其最終病逝於配流之地，四兄弟同被貶謫，流散四方。物理上的破壞同樣深遠：藤原京在戰後成為廢墟，近江與山城一帶的交通格局為之改變，平城京的宮殿與官署也在同一時期急速衰敗，二十餘年後的平安遷都因此多了一分推力。人事上，叛亂反而替藤原氏的另一支掃清了障礙，良房一族日後執政，仲麻呂之女敦子更嫁惟宗正守，育出藤原忠實一系，攝政政治的雛形就此成形。對軍制而言，靠政變、私兵與鄉族動員起家的做法被證明可行，此後數百年的武人政治由此開端。
impactEn: This was the last great civil war of the Nara age and it rewrote the politics of the following decade. The court used the rising as the pretext for a policy of honouring the Confucians and disparaging the Buddhists, for the order returning monks and nuns to lay life, for the confiscation of temple lands and for the reckoning of the temples around Heijō-kyō; Gyōshin raised armed monks in resistance and was executed when the attempt failed, and for a time the Buddhist foundation of the Nara court collapsed. The policy lasted until Emperor Uda repealed it in Jōwa 2 (835), the year in which Nagate and Uona were restored. Nakamaro himself was captured, stripped of rank and exiled, first to Izumo and then to Awaji, and the Shoku Nihongi has it that he died of illness in the place of his exile; his four brothers were demoted and scattered in the same stroke. The physical ruin was no less deep. Fujiwara-kyō lay in ashes afterwards, the pattern of roads through Ōmi and Yamashiro was altered, and the palace and public offices of Heijō-kyō were themselves decaying in the same period, so that the move of the capital to Heijin twenty years later had one more push behind it. In personal terms the rising cleared the way for another branch of the Fujiwara: the line of Nagafusa would one day take power, and Nakamaro's daughter Atsuko married Masanobu of the Kimi clan and bore the line of Fujiwara no Tadayoshi, so that the embryo of the regency system took shape here. As for the military, the rising demonstrated that a coup built on private soldiers and local kin was workable, and the long age of warrior politics began at this point.
result: 結果是叛軍在九月二十八日夜被一舉平定。藤原仲麻呂在逃亡中被擒，押送至京師後遭貶謫、配流，先後流放於出雲與淡路，最終死於流所；其四兄弟亦同時被流放，數十名叛軍首腦在木津川奧津被沈氾處死，藤原京在這一夜之後化為焦土，叛軍經營的都城據點消失。奈良朝廷的權威卻也同時被削去一層：光靠律令與敕書的國家機器，連自己的宮門都守不住，而被拉來的十四萬大軍中，實到者寥寥，一夜之間散盡。從長遠看，結果是藤原氏的內部重組與攝政體制的鞏固、奈良末期短暫的崇儒政策、佛教在中央的短暫退潮，以及平城京與藤原京雙雙衰敗所引導出的平安遷都。對日本而言，這是一場在四天之內決定了誰能握兵、誰能發出詔書的內戰；至於本站配上的羅馬重步兵，它提醒的則是同類兵種背後那套常備軍、補給線與編制制度——正是奈良朝廷當時最缺乏、也最需要學會的東西。
resultEn: The outcome was that the rebels were crushed in a single night on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. Fujiwara no Nakamaro was taken as he fled, brought to the capital, stripped of his offices and exiled, first to Izumo and then to Awaji, where he ultimately died; his four brothers were exiled with him, and several dozen of the rebel leaders were drowned at the Oku-tsu of the Kizu river. Fujiwara-kyō was a ruin of fire by the end of that night and the rebel base inside the capital was gone. The authority of the Nara court, however, was diminished by the same stroke: a state machinery resting on ritsuryō law and written orders could not even hold its own palace gates, and of the hundred and forty thousand men called in, scarcely any arrived and the few who did scattered within a night. In the longer view the result was the internal reconstitution of the Fujiwara and the consolidation of the regency system, the short-lived turn towards Confucianism at the end of the Nara age, the temporary retreat of Buddhism from the centre, and the move of the capital to Heijin that followed the decline of both Heijō-kyō and Fujiwara-kyō. For Japan this was a civil war that decided in four days who would hold the troops and who would issue the edicts. The Roman legionary on the card is a reminder of the other side of that ledger — the standing army, the supply line and the disciplined order behind a heavy infantry arm, precisely the things the Nara court lacked and had most need to learn.
